narrative:
This window was directed by the custodian: merge two session branches, supervise the first CI run, create labels, enable Discussions.

The merges are done and the CI gate passed. What dominates the window is what supervising the run surfaced -- four deficiencies, D-31 through D-34, three of them found in work merged during this same window and one of them caused by an edit made during it.

The causal chain is worth preserving because each step was ordinary. Repairing a D-29 citation changed a prompt file's digest. build_capture_ui.py embeds that digest into the published capture page. That generator was documented as running in rebuild.py -- acceptance criterion A10 of the T-13 design -- and was not. So rebuild exited 0, git status was clean, CI passed, and the published prompt-transport instrument carried a SHA-256 that did not match the artifact it named. Nothing misbehaved; a wiring claim was recorded as satisfied without being satisfied, and every downstream check inherited the gap. That is D-33.

Auditing the repair produced D-34, which is structurally worse and was found by asking what the append-only claim actually rests on. The manifest verifies the TIP. A single commit that edits raw material and re-anchors the manifest around the new bytes is self-consistent, and every check in this repository passes it -- demonstrated on a clone before being filed. 'Raw material is never edited after commit' is this corpus's central claim and nothing enforced the second half of that sentence. The control is against the custodian and any session holding credentials, which is uncomfortable and is the point.

D-32 came from the merge itself: two sessions filed different defects as D-29 because both read the register, saw D-28, and incremented, and nothing anywhere says how a number is claimed. The register is the one artifact every track appends to by design, which makes it the one artifact HANDOFF's disjoint-territory model cannot protect.

Three things this window got wrong and corrected: two test cases that asserted the wrong property and passed for the wrong reason until they were run, and one claim inside D-32 that was false in the flattering direction. All three were caught by execution rather than by reading, which is the same lesson the register keeps recording.

An unplanned control appeared. GitHub declared a major Actions and Pages outage at 15:22Z, before any run in this window. Under the newly split arrangement, verify passed every gate while deploy could not complete -- the commit verified, publication unavailable, two separate facts. Under the previous single-job design the integrity checks could not have executed at all, and the run would have shown red against the gate. Nobody designed that test.

What is NOT done: fifteen labels and two seed discussions, both blocked on token scope and both with their artifacts committed rather than held in this session. Branch protection on main is the one outstanding item that is not cosmetic -- D-34's check reads git history, and a force-push discards the history it reads.
